blurb: An original site for 7 Wells Indies, the Be'er-Sheva indie game dev community, built with the creative attitude of the classic Eye4U Flash site as the bar. Be'er Sheva means "well of seven" — so the site is a night desert with seven wells you descend into. Six are the community's real channels. The seventh is dry.

waves.title: Reference study + engine
waves.summary: Before building anything: a Playwright capture harness, then the actual Eye4U site captured live through the Wayback Machine's Ruffle Flash emulator — so the creative direction comes from the real artifact rather than a description of it.

pieces.title: What Eye4U actually does
pieces.note: Captured live, not from memory. The intro is a performance edited on beats: enormous flat vector shapes slamming through a full-bleed frame, three colours at a time, a 9px 'skip' against a screen-filling starburst. The nav is a diagram, not a menu — a photographic eye looks at an arc of beads. Three doors only. Takeaways: stage-not-document, giant flat shapes, cut-on-beat, committed palettes, identity-as-character, scale contrast, few doors.

pieces.title: Capture harness + engine substrate
pieces.note: tools/cap.mjs drives the real running site: screenshots, webm clips, and tiled contact sheets of N frames so motion can be judged as a storyboard. Engine is vanilla ES modules — scene router with hash deep-linking, WebAudio synth voices (no audio files), canvas layer helper, seeded PRNG, film grain, persisted visitor state. No build step, no framework, no external assets beyond Google Fonts.
